suspicions.claim: Website field is now escaped with quote=False instead of quote=True, so double quotes in website URLs are no longer escaped to "
suspicions.trigger: Send JSON with website containing a double quote (e.g., 'https://example.com"') and check the response body's website field for escaped double quotes Send each of these values: "https://example.com\""
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe s1: user-basic' sent a website without double quotes; probe 'probe-s1' sent a website with a double quote but both base and head returned 400 Bad Request, so the route was not reached with triggering input.

suspicions.claim: Email field is now escaped with quote=False instead of quote=True, so double quotes in email addresses are no longer escaped to "
suspicions.trigger: Send JSON with email containing a double quote (e.g., 'test"@example.com') and check the response body's email field for escaped double quotes Send each of these values: "test\"@example.com"
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe-s2' sent email "test\"@example.com" to POST /new?uri=/blog/hello-world and both base and head answered 201 with identical response bodies, showing no behavior change.

suspicions.claim: Edit comment action no longer escapes author/email/website fields, so double quotes in these fields are no longer escaped to "
suspicions.trigger: Send JSON with author, email, or website containing a double quote (e.g., 'author: "Max Rant"') and check the response body's edited fields for escaped double quotes Send each of these values: "author: \"Max Rant\""
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe-s3' attempted PUT /id/XSS test with author containing double quotes but both base and head returned 0 InvalidURL due to a space in the URL path, so the edit route was not reached with triggering input.
